Halter's component suppliers are predominantly based across Asia. The components they produce have to be right before they ever reach our contract manufacturers. When something is wrong, we need someone on the ground who can get to the root cause fast, push through to a real fix, and prevent it from happening again.
The Supplier Quality Principal is Halter's senior technical authority embedded in Asia. You'll lead highly technical supplier audits, own complex quality problem-solving at our suppliers, and work directly with both suppliers and Halter's design teams to ensure that what comes off a supplier's production line meets the standard we set.

You'll operate with a high degree of autonomy, covering a portfolio of suppliers across the region and acting as the technical bridge between our Asia supply base and the Halter team in Auckland.
This is not a compliance role. Ticking audit checkboxes and filing reports is not what this job is about. The best person for this role is someone who goes deep: who can walk a production line and immediately identify what's controlling quality and what isn't, who can sit with a supplier's engineers and work through a failure mode from first principles, and who knows the difference between a corrective action that actually solves a problem and one that just looks good on paper.
You'll report to the Head of Supplier Quality and work closely with Halter's hardware design and operations teams. When there's a quality issue in Asia that needs solving, you're the person we call.
You'll be measured on the technical quality of audits, the speed and effectiveness of issue resolution at suppliers, and your ability to build supplier capability over time.

Technical Supplier Auditing
Lead technically rigorous audits of Halter's component suppliers across Asia, going well beyond system compliance to assess process control, measurement capability, and the reliability of how suppliers actually build and inspect parts.
Identify the real drivers of quality performance at a supplier, not just the documented procedures, and develop clear, prioritised findings that distinguish between critical risks and cosmetic gaps.
Conduct pre-qualification audits of new suppliers, assessing their technical capability and readiness to meet Halter's design and quality requirements before commitments are made.
Run periodic surveillance audits to verify that corrective actions have been implemented effectively and that quality performance is being sustained.
Develop and continuously improve Halter's audit methodology and supplier assessment criteria, ensuring audits capture what actually matters for component quality.
Technical Problem Solving
Own the resolution of complex quality issues at suppliers, using first-principles analysis to identify root cause and drive effective corrective actions rather than superficial fixes.
When a production failure or OQC rejection occurs, lead rapid on-site analysis with supplier engineers and Halter's design team to understand the failure mode, assess risk to in-flight inventory, and define the fastest path to resolution.
Work with suppliers to improve their process controls, measurement systems, and inspection methods so that quality issues are caught and corrected at source, not downstream.
Coach supplier engineering teams to develop their own capability for root cause analysis and corrective action, building their ability to self-solve rather than depend on Halter for every issue.
Escalate issues clearly and early when resolution is taking too long, a supplier is not engaging in good faith, or a quality risk to production is emerging.
Quality Assurance Specifications
Implement and maintain Halter's quality assurance specifications at suppliers, ensuring specifications are understood, accepted, and consistently applied across the production process.
Work with Halter's hardware design team and the Head of Supplier Quality to refine QA specifications where field experience, audit findings, or supplier feedback reveals gaps or ambiguity.
Ensure that when designs evolve, updated specifications are communicated to suppliers, implemented correctly, and re-validated before affected parts re-enter supply.
Challenge specifications that are unclear, unmeasurable, or misaligned with what suppliers can realistically control, bringing engineering and operations teams to a better standard.
Part Approval and Ongoing Compliance
Support supplier-side part approval activities, ensuring new and revised components are formally validated against Halter's specifications before production release.
Maintain a clear picture of approval status and open quality issues across the suppliers in your portfolio, tracking corrective actions to closure and flagging risks to supply continuity.
Collaborate with the Head of Contract Manufacturing Quality when parts that pass supplier OQC fail IQC at our contract manufacturers, working to determine whether root cause sits with the supplier process, the OQC criteria, or the incoming inspection.
Supplier Development
Build genuine working relationships with quality and engineering counterparts at key suppliers, creating the trust and technical credibility that allows hard conversations to happen fast.
Identify where suppliers have systemic capability gaps and develop structured improvement plans that address root cause, not symptoms.
Share Halter's standards, expectations, and technical knowledge with suppliers in a way that builds their capability over time rather than creating dependency.

15 or more years of experience in supplier quality or manufacturing quality for complex electromechanical hardware, with a proven track record of solving technically difficult quality problems at suppliers.
Deep manufacturing and process engineering knowledge. You understand how parts are made, what drives process variation, and how to identify whether a supplier's process is actually in control.

You’ll translate product behavior and real-world use cases into structured, reproducible test procedures and build test environments that allow failures to be reliably reproduced and diagnosed.

We’re looking for someone who combines strong systems thinking, hands-on testing skills, technical curiosity, and a rigorous approach to reproducing and diagnosing failures across multiple components.

Design end-to-end test coverage: Develop structured test plans and reproducible procedures for user journeys, realistic usage patterns, edge cases, degraded conditions, and failure scenarios across devices, services, connectivity, and accessories.

Reproduce failures and diagnose systems: Reproduce complex failures, isolate contributing components, collect logs and telemetry, and provide engineers with clear reproduction steps and supporting evidence.

About Supercell
Supercell is a games company from Helsinki, Finland, with offices also in San Francisco, Seoul, Shanghai, and London. You might know us as the makers of Hay Day, Clash of Clans, Boom Beach, Clash Royale, and Brawl Stars . Our mission is to create great games that as many people as possible play for years and that are remembered forever.
So, how do we make great games? By putting together the best teams and giving them the freedom and independence to succeed. And by taking risks, failing, sharing learnings , and killing lots of projects.
Hey, You Might Love It Here!

Wishing you all the best,

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

Anthropic is building and securing data center capacity at an unprecedented pace, and the power and cooling equipment that goes into those sites — switchgear, UPS, generators, transformers, busway, chillers, CDUs, air handlers, pumps and piping skids — is long-lead, high-value, and unforgiving of defects. A single nonconformance discovered at site can cost weeks of schedule.
We're hiring a Manufacturing Quality Engineer to own quality at the source: inside our OEMs' and integrators' factories. You will qualify suppliers, define acceptance criteria, witness factory acceptance tests, drive corrective action to closure, and make sure equipment leaves the factory complete, conforming, documented, and ready to install. You are the person who catches the problem in Ohio before it becomes a problem in Texas.
This is a hands-on individual-contributor role on the Compute DC Infrastructure team, partnering daily with Electrical and Mechanical Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, Construction, and Commissioning. It is not a supplier-relationship-management role and not a people-management role — the emphasis is technical quality engineering at manufacturing facilities.

Lead quality qualification of new and existing suppliers of power and cooling equipment, including on-site process audits, capability assessments, and manufacturing readiness reviews (MRRs) ahead of production release.
Translate Anthropic engineering specifications into supplier-facing quality requirements: inspection and test plans (ITPs), acceptance criteria, witness/hold points, and documentation deliverables.
Partner with Strategic Sourcing to embed quality requirements, Supplier Quality Agreements, and FAT/documentation expectations into RFPs and contracts.
Factory acceptance and in-process quality
Plan, witness, and sign off factory acceptance tests (FATs) for electrical gear (switchgear, UPS, transformers, gensets, busway, PDUs) and mechanical systems (chillers, CDUs, CRAH/fan walls, dry coolers, pumps, piping skids), including functional, performance, and integrated-system testing.
Conduct in-process and pre-shipment inspections at supplier facilities; verify build-to-print conformance, workmanship, labeling, and traceability.
Review and approve supplier test reports, quality data packages, and turnover documentation; ensure equipment ships complete and installation-ready.
Nonconformance and corrective action
Own the nonconformance (NCR) and deviation process for factory-found issues; lead containment, disposition, and root-cause analysis using 8D, 5-Why, FMEA, and fault-tree methods.
Drive supplier corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) to verified closure with measurable, sustained improvement.
Investigate field-reported defects that trace back to manufacturing, and feed lessons learned into supplier requirements, ITPs, and future RFPs.
Metrics and continuous improvement
Define and track supplier quality KPIs — first-pass FAT yield, defect rate, NCR aging, on-time documentation, supplier scorecards — and report them in quarterly supplier business reviews.
Apply SPC and statistical analysis to supplier process data to identify systemic risk before it reaches a FAT.
Help build the quality framework for a rapidly scaling, multi-supplier, multi-region equipment pipeline — templates, checklists, audit standards, and the operating rhythm around them.

6–10+ years of quality engineering, manufacturing quality, or supplier quality experience in electrical or mechanical equipment manufacturing, mission-critical infrastructure, or a comparable regulated/high-consequence industry.
Hands-on experience with at least one side of the data center equipment stack — medium/low-voltage switchgear, UPS, generators, transformers, busway, or chillers, CDUs, air handlers, pumps — and the curiosity to come up to speed fast on the other.
Proven record planning and witnessing FATs and conducting supplier audits, with the judgment to know when to hold a shipment and when to accept with deviation.
Deep fluency in structured problem-solving and quality tools: 8D, RCA, FMEA, SPC, control plans, PPAP or equivalent.
Able to read electrical one-lines, P&IDs, and mechanical drawings and check a build against them.
Strong technical writing — you produce ITPs, audit reports, and NCR packages that stand on their own.
Comfortable operating with high autonomy and ambiguity, and communicating clearly to engineers, suppliers, and leadership.
Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Mechanical, Manufacturing, or Industrial Engineering, or equivalent experience.

Experience with hyperscale or AI data center equipment supply chains, or with OFCI (owner-furnished, contractor-installed) delivery models.
Familiarity with liquid-cooling systems (CDUs, manifolds, quick disconnects) and the cleanliness, pressure, and leak-test regimes they require.
Working knowledge of relevant standards: UL 891/1558/1778, IEEE C37, NEMA, AHRI 550/590, ASHRAE 90.4, ASME B31.x, ISO 9001 auditing.
ASQ CQE/CQA, Six Sigma Green/Black Belt, or lead-auditor certification.
Experience standing up a supplier quality function or QMS from a small base.
Proficiency with QMS/ERP platforms and data tools (SQL, Power BI, or similar).

As Axon’s Supplier Quality Engineer, you will be responsible for providing Supplier Quality Development support for all Axon products, including Conducted Electrical Weapons, Cartridges, Counter Drone devices and accessories.

You will be a key technical leader responsible for working with suppliers, in cooperation with Axon Design Engineering, Supplier Quality and Supply Chain. You will evaluate and select qualified suppliers. You will lead efforts to measure and improve supplier performance. This work will positively impact the quality of new and existing products.

Specifically, you will help reduce PPMs, lower costs related to poor quality, and improve on-time delivery. Axon is a dynamic, fast-paced environment and we welcome new ideas, team spirit and cooperation across departments. We offer career growth plans for our employees and provide technical training and learning as needed.

Location: Onsite at our Scottsdale, AZ office
Reports to: Manager, Supplier Quality Development
Direct Reports: N/A
Audit contract manufacturing partners and suppliers with critical manufacturing & inspection processes, policies and procedures to ensure performance and quality standards conform to established Axon Quality requirements.
·Engage in selection and evaluation activities of potential new suppliers (including CM/JDM/ODM) and conduct onsite auditing of the supplier to assess quality and/or process related requirements. Participate in Supplier quote reviews to provide input on process related costs.
Ensure flow down of Axon Supplier Quality requirements to its supply base.
Ensure New Product Introduction (NPI) takes place in accordance with criteria and inspection plans set up and managed by Axon Program Management, Design and Quality, and in accordance with Supply Chain purchase order requirements and clauses.
Lead DFx reviews and product/process qualification by supplier (PPAP/FAIR), monitor supplier process FMEA and production control plan (PCP), and advise continuous improvement collaboration efforts.
Assess supplier inspection capabilities on-site (IQC/OQC/IPQC). Assist in generating appropriate inspection plans, conduct measurement method evaluation and correlation studies, and assess any inspection and process capability studies provided by suppliers (Cpk, Ppk, Gage R&R)
Evaluate Axon and supplier engineering drawings, specifications, special processes and related purchasing requirements for processes, product fabrication and inspection plans, and communicate/coordinate acceptance with Axon Design, Manufacturing and Quality.
Participate in measuring, reporting, and correcting supplier quality performance, control processing system anomalies, and non-conforming processes and products.
Issue Supplier Corrective Action Requests (SCARs), and Non-Conformance Material Reports (NCMRs) to resolve issues. Review and evaluate supplier RCA and CAPA to assure robustness of identified causes and defined actions.
If required, participate in creating remedial activities for suppliers displaying low quality performance based on defective PPMs and non-conformance frequencies, in coordination with Axon Supply Chain and Quality.
Communicate and monitor any implemented corrective action, improvement plans and lessons learnt at the supplier after non-conformance events.
Provide feedback, data and metrics regarding supplier quality performance level to Operations, Finance, Engineering and Supply Chain.

Dedrone systems sit at the bleeding edge of counter-UAS (CUAS) capability. You'll design and execute the test strategies that prove them out, across hardware/software integration, networking, active and passive detection, computer vision, RF mitigation/defeat, environmental durability, and automated regression.

You'll be the engineer who understands the entire system and its nuances end to end: you'll determine whether a system has what it takes to meet the objective, build the tooling to evaluate it against live drone threats, and be the one who can reproduce the issue nobody else can.

Your job is to make sure the systems our customers rely on hold up in the real world, against real threats, at the forefront of technology.
In this role the drone is the threat . What's under test is the CUAS stack - detect, track, identify, and defeat - along with the sensors, software, integrations, and platforms that deliver it.

Own system-level test strategy for one or more CUAS product lines, from early prototype through production and field deployment.
Design and execute integration test plans across the full stack: RF sensors, radar, EO/IR and acoustic sensors, computer vision, RF detection/DF, jamming and mitigation/defeat, networking, radios, and third-party system integrations.
Plan and execute field test campaigns at the range - flying threat-representative target drones against the system and executing live detect–track–ID–defeat runs.
Build and maintain test tooling, automation, and instrumented data capture and reduction, regression automation, and HIL / RF-chamber / environmental setups for sensor and platform hardware.
Collect, analyze, and report test metrics, turn field data into clear insights, recommendations, and event reports for PM, engineering, and leadership.
Evaluate third-party and integrated systems against defined acceptance criteria to determine whether a system or integration meets the cut.
Triage complex multi-system failures across HW, FW, SW, RF, and network; reproduce intermittent field issues others can't.
Partner with various Dedrone teams during design reviews to bake in testability early.
Help shape the System Test and Evaluation discipline across Dedrone.

Required
BS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Aerospace, or a related field — or equivalent hands-on experience. We actively welcome non-traditional paths: prior technician, electrician, military technical-trade experience followed by a degree is a strength, not a gap.
5–8 years across system test, system integration, field test & evaluation, or hands-on technical roles (military or industry) on complex electromechanical and RF systems.
Hands-on with at least two of: HW/SW integration testing, RF/wireless validation, environmental/reliability testing, test automation, electrical system testing, radar testing, EO/IR or camera testing, acoustic sensing.
Demonstrated ability to debug across the stack - hardware, electrical, RF, network, and software.
Some experience in software / automation
Comfortable owning field operations and translating raw test data into decisions stakeholders can act on.
U.S. person defined as a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent residents (Green Card holders)
Approximately 50% field time

CUAS, EW/SIGINT, RF, Cameras, Radar or other mission-critical / safety-critical system experience.
RF and wireless depth: DF, spectrum analysis, and the protocols drones live on (sub-GHz proprietary, Wi-Fi, LTE/5G, Bluetooth), plus jamming/mitigation.
Familiarity with UAS.
Experience with automated test frameworks.

We're looking for someone who gets a kick out of turning "someone should really automate this" into a working tool by next week. You'll sit at the intersection of Lifecycle, Sales, and AI — building the agents, workflows, and internal products that let Clara prospect, sell, and onboard faster and smarter than a headcount-only approach ever could.

This isn't a "use AI to write better emails" role. It's a build role. You'll ship things: SDR co-pilots, outbound agents, lifecycle automations, onboarding flows — and you'll own whether they actually move pipeline and activation, not just whether they're clever.

Build AI-powered prospecting & SDR tooling: design and ship agents/workflows that find, qualify, and engage prospects, and that get meetings on AEs' calendars — using tools like Amplemarket, Clay, HubSpot, and LLM APIs, glued together with n8n or custom code.
Own lifecycle automation end to end: build and iterate on onboarding, activation, and retention flows across email, WhatsApp, and push, using Customer.io and our internal data stack, with AI doing the heavy lifting on personalization, timing, and content generation.
Design the SDR-to-AE handoff as a system, not a manual process: instrument lead scoring, routing, and handoff logic so reps spend time on conversations, not admin.
Prototype fast, validate faster: you're expected to go from idea to working internal tool in days, test it against real pipeline/activation metrics, kill what doesn't work, and scale what does.
Partner cross-functionally: work directly with Sales, SDR leadership, Lifecycle, and Data/Eng to identify where automation unlocks the most value, and to make sure what you build actually gets adopted.
Turn data into iteration: use Metabase, HubSpot, and Customer.io data to measure what your builds are actually doing to CAC payback, meetings booked, activation rate, and pipeline generated — and report on it in plain, honest terms.
We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Strong written and verbal communication in English; ability to explain what you built and why it matters to non-technical stakeholders and executives.
A bias toward building and testing over planning — you'd rather ship a rough version this week than a perfect spec next month.

Background in Lifecycle Marketing, RevOps, Sales Engineering, Product, or Software Engineering (any of these paths is fine — we care about what you've built, not your job title history).
Direct experience with sales engagement/AI prospecting tools (Amplemarket, Clay, Apollo, or similar).

We are looking for a Hardware Signal Quality Test Engineer to join our San Francisco team. As Oura’s first HSQT engineer in San Francisco, you will help establish and grow local validation capability for Oura Ring sensors.

You will contribute to hardware validation projects, execute hands-on testing, analyze sensor data, investigate issues, and communicate actionable results. You’ll work within established global processes while helping adapt practical test methods and workflows to the San Francisco lab.

You will collaborate closely with testing teams , Science, Hardware Engineering, Firmware and Embedded Software Engineering, and Product Quality.
This is a hybrid position based in San Francisco, Bay Area.

Contribute to sensor validation cycles for Oura’s next-generation hardware products, executing defined test activities and helping evaluate signal quality across relevant sensor domains.
Contribute to test planning and adapt test methods and tools to evaluate physical and physiological signals (e.g., motion, optical, electrical, and thermal).
Analyze sensor data and performance using Python and appropriate data-analysis methods, identifying patterns and extracting actionable insights.
Conduct hands-on testing in the lab and, where appropriate, real-world field environments; identify unexpected behavior and support root-cause investigations.
Deliver clear, data-driven reports and findings to cross-functional stakeholders, supporting hardware, algorithms, firmware, and product-quality decisions.
Contribute to improvements in test capabilities, documentation, automation, and reporting, helping establish repeatable sensor-validation practices at the San Francisco site.

Required
Bachelor’s degree in Biomedical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
3+ years of relevant hands-on experience in sensor testing, hardware validation, laboratory measurement, research, or a related engineering environment.
Working experience with Python for data analysis, test tooling, or automation; willingness to continue developing these skills.
Basic familiarity with analog or digital signal analysis and processing.
Basic understanding of electronics, sensors, or embedded systems.
Innovative mindset with a strong interest in the latest sensor technologies.
Proactive and diligent, with the ability to take ownership of scoped work, seek guidance when needed, and communicate results clearly to stakeholders.
Strong collaboration skills, able to work effectively across disciplines and time zones.
Excellent problem-solving abilities and an analytical approach to technical challenges.
Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.
Willingness and ability to travel to Oura sites and contract manufacturing facilities as needed.

Knowledge of human physiology and physiological signals.
Experience with electronics and implementing different test fixtures
Background in hardware testing and debugging, including software interfaces.
Familiarity with regulatory testing processes for medical or other wearable devices.
Work Model
Location: Fully on-site in San Francisco, Bay Area.
Collaboration with global hardware, firmware, test engineering, and manufacturing teams.
Occasional travel may be required (to suppliers or Finland).

We are looking for a Senior Product Quality Engineer, EE to join our Product Quality team in San Francisco, California. In this role you will lead Early Field Failure Analysis (EFFA), field quality, and product safety for the Oura Ring, covering both products currently in mass production and earlier generations still in members’ hands.

You will determine why electrical failures occur in the field, confirm the mechanism behind them, and drive the design, process, supplier, and test changes required to prevent them from recurring.
Job responsibilities include leading electrical failure analysis on returned units, building serial-level evidence packages from manufacturing, test, and telemetry data, and establishing commonality across build, supplier, revision, and geography. You will define containment and escalation for field safety issues, direct corrective action with our contract manufacturers (CMs) and suppliers, and verify effectiveness against field and factory data before an action is considered closed.
A core objective of this role is closing the quality loop. You will convert confirmed field and factory findings into design, DFMEA, test coverage, and component selection inputs for NPI programs, so that mechanisms identified on shipping products are designed out of the next generation. This requires close partnership with Electrical Engineering, Firmware, Reliability, Manufacturing, Supplier Quality, Data, and Member Experience.
This role spans the bench, the data, and the factory floor. Strong electrical engineering fundamentals, hands-on failure analysis capability, and practical data analysis skill are all essential for success in this role.
This is a US Hybrid role based in the San Francisco Bay Area, with an in-office requirement of three days per week.

Own electrical Early Field Failure Analysis (EFFA) for Oura Ring products, from returned unit intake and evidence review through technical disposition, confirmed mechanism, and closure
Lead field quality and safety investigations for battery, charging, and power-related issues, including risk assessment, containment and escalation decisions, and the supporting technical rationale for Reliability, Regulatory, and Member Experience
Direct non-destructive-first analysis workflows covering received-condition documentation, electrical characterization, ring diagnostics, optical inspection, and imaging prior to any destructive analysis
Isolate failure mechanisms across power, battery, charging, sensor, clock, connectivity, interconnect, and leakage-related faults to the component, material, or process level using DMM, oscilloscope, current measurement, thermal imaging, micro-probing, and X-ray/CT
Build serial-level evidence packages combining product configuration, hardware and firmware revision, manufacturing genealogy, factory test history, telemetry, and diagnostic records against the member-reported symptom
Analyze field, factory, and FA data to establish commonality across manufacturing site, build lot, supplier, component, ring size, hardware and firmware revision, product age, geography, and diagnostic signature
Distinguish reported symptom from failed function and confirmed mechanism, documenting supporting and contradicting evidence, remaining open questions, and confidence in the disposition
Drive corrective action with CMs and suppliers, including factory containment, process control updates, inspection and test coverage, design and firmware changes, and additional reliability validation
Verify corrective action effectiveness against before-and-after field, factory, reliability, or component data prior to closure
Feed confirmed field and factory findings into NPI through design and DFMEA reviews, component and supplier selection, test coverage definition, traceability requirements, and reliability planning
Partner with Data and Software teams on data ingestion, SQL and Python analysis, dashboards, and triage logic to convert confirmed mechanisms into leading indicators and proactive capture criteria
Establish FA methods, standard operating procedures, equipment requirements, and reporting templates, and build repeatable capability across Oura’s regional labs and CM partners
Present findings to engineering and quality leadership, clearly separating observation, hypothesis, confirmed mechanism, corrective action, and open risk
You are a technical leader who insists on evidence and is comfortable with ambiguity. You understand that a passing functional test is not the same as a robust product, and that the purpose of failure analysis is not to explain a single return but to prevent the same mechanism from reaching future members.

We are seeking a highly skilled Senior Software Test Engineer to join our team. In this role, you will be responsible for planning, implementing, and executing tests for end to end features, data flows and algorithms the power core Oura experiences across mobile apps (iOS & Android) and cloud services.

You will play a key role in ensuring product quality by driving test automation efforts, reporting issues and bugs, and collaborating closely with developers to debug and resolve complex issues.

You will also own and refine testing capabilities, processes, and methodologies, contributing to continuous improvements in our test capabilities and work closely with cross-functional teams across the US and Finland to deliver high-quality products.

Test Strategy and Planning
Develop comprehensive test strategies and plans for end to end features including mobile applications, backend services and data/algorithmic solutions.
Define testing objectives, scope, and success criteria for each test phase ensuring coverage for complex user scenarios (e.g., onboarding, sleep and readiness insights, activity tracking, notifications, subscription flows).
Collaborate with Product, Science, and Firmware teams to understand feature requirements, data/algorithm behavior, and any regulatory or privacy considerations.
Test Execution and Reporting
Execute manual and automated tests, analyze test results, and report defects, issues, and bugs in a clear, concise manner.
Validate data flow and algorithm accuracy, ensuring inputs from the ring and backend translate correctly to user‑facing insights in the app.
Perform regression, integration, and exploratory testing on new features, experiments, and releases across platforms.Use and Implement big data monitoring against acceptance criteria.
Visualize data and metrics (coverage, defect trends, pass rates) to communicate test coverage and quality status to stakeholders.
Automation and Continuous Integration
Implement, maintain, and enhance test automation frameworks for mobile and API testing using for e.g., Pytest, Appium.
Integrate automated testing in CI/CD pipelines (e.g., GitHub Actions, Gitlab CI, Jenkins) to support continuous testing & fast feedback.
Ensure regression suites for ring and app experiences are stable, reliable, and provide high‑value coverage for core health and engagement features.
Contribute to test data management and environment setup, using emulators, simulators, and test rings where applicable.
Collaboration and Debugging
Work closely with developers, product managers, and other stakeholders to debug issues and ensure timely resolutions.
Participate in planning, design, and review discussions to bring a quality perspective early in the development lifecycle.
Advocate for best practices in QA and continuously improve testing methods, processes, and tools.
Quality Assurance Ownership
Take ownership of product quality, driving testing initiatives that ensure high reliability and performance.
Champion quality standards, ensuring all teams adhere to best practices and processes.
Maintain clear, up‑to‑date test documentation (test plans, test cases, automation coverage, known issues) for your feature areas.
Process Improvement
Evaluate and introduce new tools and methodologies for efficient, scalable, and robust testing.
Provide mentorship and guidance to junior test team members.
Advanced Testing & Technology Exploration
Explore the use of AI-driven testing approaches and tools, especially in the context of LLMs.
Conduct performance testing to verify that products meet performance benchmarks.
This is a Hybrid role out of our San Francisco office.

Extensive QA and Test Automation Experience - Minimum 8+ years of Proven track record of designing, building, and executing automated tests for complex applications.
End-to-End Testing Experience Experience testing complex, multi-component systems (e.g., embedded software combined with mobile applications & cloud-based applications).
Domain Experience: Experience testing health, wellness, wearable, or data‑driven applications, hardware in lab environments and validating end‑to‑end user experiences. Familiarity with testing algorithms and time‑series or sensor‑driven features is a strong plus.
Experience testing embedded firmware and Bluetooth‑enabled devices (e.g., device‑to‑mobile connectivity, syncing, and reliability) is a plus
Proven experience validating wireless communication technologies. Analyzing and debugging wireless communication logs and traces to identify root causes of failures, performance issues, and edge‑case behaviors is a plus.
Automation Frameworks & ToolsHands-on experience with frameworks such as Pytest, Appium, Playwright (or similar).

CI/CD ExpertiseFamiliarity with CI/CD tools such as Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and the best practices for continuous testing.
Analytical and Troubleshooting SkillsAbility to identify root causes of complex issues quickly using logs, metrics, and data, and drive solutions with cross‑functional teams.
Communication & CollaborationStrong interpersonal skills with the ability to work cross-functionally with developers, product teams, and other stakeholders to ensure shared understanding of requirements and quality goals.
Experience with LLMs and AI-driven dev/test tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor)

As a Product Quality Engineer at Peloton, you will be responsible for ensuring our hardware products are designed, manufactured, and tested to a high quality standard so that our members can continue to access Peloton’s fitness experiences throughout the life of their products.

You will need to identify major risks starting from the earliest project stages and define quality plans to mitigate and control these risks prior to launch.

You will also be responsible for leading investigations of top issues from root cause analysis through to corrective action, and documenting learnings to prevent recurrence of similar issues in the future.

This role will work closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Service and Repair, and other teams starting from concept through to mass production and sustaining.

Partner with multi-functional teams through early risk assessments (using FMEA/NUD processes and past lessons learned). Implement mitigation strategies and test plans to address and close potential risks.
Lead response to quality escalations and drive complex issues to closure using methodical 8D/RCCA approaches.
Define, implement, and audit quality processes at our FATP sites to ensure final products meet quality targets.
Communicate Quality risks, mitigations, and next steps to the leadership team and other key stakeholders.
Influence partners to implement quality improvements for field performance.
This role requires domestic and international travel up to 30%.

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Science, or other technical discipline.
4+ years of experience in product development with 2+ years specifically in a Quality role for complex electro-mechanical products (e.g., Fitness Equipment, Medical Devices, Automotive, or Consumer Electronics).
Demonstrated understanding of NPI (New Product Introduction) cycles and how to successfully drive quality improvements during development.
Track record of resolving business-critical quality issues.
Ability to develop specifications and test plans, and translate test results into product recommendations.
Familiar with statistical data analysis and related software tools (e.g., Minitab, JMP).
Understanding of quality tools and methodologies (eg., DOE, MSA, Hypothesis testing, GR&R, CpK).
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a proven ability to build consensus and influence decisions at all levels of an organization.

Advanced Degree in Science or Engineering.
Six-Sigma Greenbelt training or certification.

As a QA Engineer, you will work with numerous disciplines to drive quality ownership across the software development life cycle, as well as helping to establish and execute team wide quality goals. It will be important for you to aggressively protect the player experience and deliver results in a high pressure, agile development environment.

You will also be accountable as the quality owner of an area or product in addition to identifying and implementing quality improvements to the team’s development process. Additionally, you may partner with and mentor remote QA teams to ensure features are delivered at a high quality bar.

Lastly, you will identify and mitigate risks to feature delivery and product quality and craft data to report on the quality of the product and update partners.
As an QA Engineer III on the Accessibility team, you will help ensure that Riot products deliver high-quality, inclusive experiences for players. You will own accessibility quality activities across the product development life cycle, partnering closely with product, engineering, design, UX, research, production, compliance, and QA teams.

This role combines hands-on accessibility validation with scalable capability building. You will perform and guide accessibility testing, help teams identify and mitigate risk, and establish repeatable practices, tools, metrics, and training that enable product teams to build accessibility into their work from the start.

You will be expected to operate as an accessibility quality subject-matter expert across one or more products or initiatives, influence decisions beyond your immediate team, and contribute to improving how accessibility quality is practiced across Riot. This role reports to the Director of Product Accessibility.

Define accessibility test approaches and integrate them into product QA strategies, test plans, regression processes, and release readiness.
Plan, execute, and guide manual and automated accessibility testing across games, web, video, and other digital experiences.
Test with assistive technologies and interaction modalities, including screen readers, keyboard navigation, controller input, and flash-rate testing tools.
Conduct accessibility audits and regression testing; translate findings into actionable user stories, defects, quality reports, and remediation guidance.
Triage and prioritize accessibility risks using player impact, severity, likelihood, product context, and release needs.
Establish quality metrics and use test results, defect trends, and player feedback to drive decisions and continuous improvement.
Create reusable guidance, tools, checklists, and training that help product teams build accessibility into planning, design, development, and testing.
Coach QA professionals, external testers, and product partners on accessibility test design, execution, and reporting.
Communicate accessibility quality status, risks, and recommendations while collaborating across distributed teams and disciplines.

5+ years of software quality assurance experience, with multiple examples of successful product or feature delivery.
Experience designing, implementing, and executing test approaches as part of an overall test strategy.
Experience with accessibility testing across digital products, games, web experiences, or comparable software.
Experience with manual testing and familiarity with automated testing approaches, tools, or frameworks.
Experience using assistive technologies, including common screen readers such as JAWS, NVDA, and VoiceOver.
Experience testing keyboard navigation and other relevant input methods or assistive technologies.
Experience performing flash-rate or photosensitivity testing, including use of tools such as Harding or PEAT, or the ability to quickly develop equivalent expertise.

Background in rocket engines, fluid components, or spacecraft propulsion systems

Experience with instrumentation, sensors, and data acquisition systems

Based out of Rocket Lab's new site in Albuquerque, NM as part of the SolAero Technologies acquisition, the Senior Quality Engineer is responsible for promoting a quality culture focused on continuous improvement and innovation across all aspects of the business.

This role works closely with cross-functional teams to ensure product and process excellence throughout the product lifecycle, while maintaining compliance with AS9100, customer, and internal requirements.

The Quality Engineer leads quality initiatives, manages the Quality Management System (QMS), and represents the organization in all matters related to product quality.

Promote a quality culture focused on continuous improvement and innovation to ensure the organization achieves exceptional results.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams on customer design reviews, new product development, in-process product monitoring, contract reviews, and internal specification reviews.
Monitor product performance throughout the product lifecycle, ensuring compliance with customer and internal specifications, and drive a culture of efficiency and change.
Create, monitor, and continuously improve QMS procedures, policies, work instructions, manuals, and records to ensure compliance with AS9100, customer, and internal requirements.
Represent the organization in customer service matters, including customer complaints, visits, audits, and inquiries related to product quality.
Lead quality improvements, root cause analysis, corrective actions, internal audits, and non-conformance reviews as required.
Support the Engineering Change process by participating in technical reviews to ensure changes align with customer requirements, internal standards, and manufacturing protocols.
Verify and validate that in-process and completed products meet all performance and appearance requirements.
Deploy the Quality Management System within the scope of work to support operational excellence.
Facilitate Material Review Boards, Corrective Action Boards, and Return Material Authorization processes as needed.
Create, monitor, and automate metrics for discrepancy reports, nonconformances, corrective actions, supplier quality, cost of poor quality (CoPQ), KPIs, RMAs, and other quality-related metrics.
Take necessary action when Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) do not meet expectations.
Conduct internal and supplier quality audits, identifying compliance or non-conformities per AS9100 standards.
Manage incoming supplier quality activities, including supplier on-time delivery (OTD), defect tracking, and corrective actions for performance issues.
Develop and implement sampling plans, inspection requirements, and procedures for incoming, in-process, and final product quality assurance.
Participate in meetings such as staff meetings, design meetings, project reviews, customer meetings, technical reviews, operational meetings, and audits.
Provide technical support and clarification to Quality and Manufacturing Inspection Technicians regarding documentation, product quality requirements, and non-conformance identification.
Conduct training and certification of Inspectors as needed.
Identify and document non-conformances, and participate in root cause and corrective action activities.
Exercise authority to stop processes that threaten product quality, company reputation, or employee safety.
Initiate corrective action and halt processes when major nonconformances are detected.
Travel as required for off-site testing events, customer repair trips, or program meetings

Bachelor’s degree
5+ years in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or Chemical Engineering related field
Experience implementing cross-functional projects in a technical environment.

Based out of Rocket Lab Optical Systems in Chantilly, VA, the Senior Supplier Quality Engineer I is responsible for ensuring the quality requirements for procured parts, services & processes are achieved.

Working as a liaison between our internal customers and suppliers you are a critical conduit for translating technical requirements into easy and clear specifications that suppliers can achieve.

Your exceptional communication and negotiation skills will encourage suppliers to strive for improvement, implement more robust quality processes and drive cost reduction, processes efficiency whilst enabling smooth management of the sometimes-conflicting priorities between customers & suppliers.

Embody and promote Scopely’s core tenets through your actions, communication, and leadership

Strong time management, accountability and organisational skills

Avionics Integration and Test Engineers are responsible for acceptance and qualification tests of our satellite’s electrical systems and own the Highly Accelerated Stress Screening (HASS) chambers used to screen flight hardware before launch.

Drive continuous improvement efforts to increase throughput and reduce cost to meet targets
Write automation software in Python to interact with flight hardware, test equipment, instrumentation, and production documentation

Starshield leverages SpaceX's Starlink technology and launch capability to support national security efforts. While Starlink is designed for consumer and commercial use, Starshield is designed for government use, with an initial focus on three areas: Earth observation, communications, and hosted payloads.

Designed to meet diverse mission requirements, Starshield satellites are capable of integrating a wide variety of payloads, offering unique versatility to users.

With the proven ability to iterate rapidly, SpaceX's unique full-stack approach in developing end-to-end systems, from launch vehicles to user terminals, enables the deployment of capabilities at scale with unprecedented speed.

Starshield's proliferated low-Earth orbit architecture provides inherent resiliency and constant connectivity to on-orbit assets, while SpaceX's proven rapid launch capability provides expedient and economical access to space.

s.h: LEAD ELECTRICAL TEST ENGINEER, CUSTOMER HARDWARE (STARLINK)
s.t:
SpaceX is leveraging its experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide.

We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact.

As we continue to upgrade and expand the constellation, we’re looking for best-in-class engineers to join the team.
As a Starlink Production Test Development Lead, you will lead a team of test engineers responsible for high-volume production test.

In addition to insourced products you will also work with global contract manufacturers to ensure robust quality of millions of customer-facing devices that we ship directly to end users (Starlink dishes/user terminals, Wi-Fi routers, etc.).

Our customers currently include teachers in the most remote parts of the Amazon, researchers in Antarctica, digital nomads who travel via RV, emergency responders, commercial airlines, cruise lines, and residential users who live in more rural or developing areas.

You will be responsible for the design, implementation, and verification of development, production, and reliability test solutions.

You will interact regularly with senior leadership to influence the fundamental operation of our products while collaborating with electrical, silicon, software, mechanical, and manufacturing teams to steer this project from initial concept development to full-scale production.

Lead a small team of test engineers developing fixtures, test cases and automated test solutions for our high-volume consumer phased arrays, WiFi routers, power supplies, and upcoming products
Develop and maintain Design For Test (DFT) guidelines and work with design teams to implement the guidelines on new products
Develop test strategies, perform thorough test coverage analyses, and conduct formal test strategy reviews with peer teams
Write automation software in Python to interact with units under test, test equipment, instrumentation, field data, and production documentation systems
Work closely with and consistently provide feedback to responsible design engineers, manufacturing engineers, and test lab teams to drive design or infrastructure improvements to increase product quality and yield
Challenge assumptions and work to find simple solutions to complex problems

Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering or other engineering discipline
5+ years of experience with hardware development or electronics test engineering (internship and extracurricular experience is applicable)
5+ years of object-oriented programming experience

2+ years of experience with technical leadership
Experience analyzing circuits, developing functional test plans, and performing test coverage analysis
Experience designing and troubleshooting PCBAs
Experience with test equipment and measurement techniques to verify and validate product requirements (oscilloscope, multimeter, electronic load, spectrum analyzer, network analyzer, vector signal generator, source measurement unit, etc.)
Understanding of electrical schematics and electronics manufacturing to analyze and improve test coverage
Understanding of metrology, sources of measurement error, and uncertainty analysis
Experience interacting with repositories using Git commands
Thorough understanding of electronics reliability and failure mechanisms
Understanding and experience in environmental testing such as HALT/HASS, thermal, vibration and TVAC
Strong understanding of computers and programming languages (Python, C/C++)
Demonstrated ability to work in a highly cross-functional role
Basic understanding of networking concepts, Virtual LANs (VLANs) and Network Address Translation (NAT)
Ability to work extended hours or weekends as needed for mission critical deadlines

s.h: MANUFACTURING AUTOMATION ENGINEER, CHAMBER AND NOZZLE (RAPTOR)
s.t:
SpaceX is seeking an engineer with deep expertise in manufacturing automation to create the machines that build the Raptor engine’s combustion chamber and nozzle. These components feature some of the most complex geometries in rocket propulsion — including intricate regenerative cooling channels, thin-walled high-temperature alloys, and tight-tolerance surfaces that must survive extreme thermal and pressure cycles across hundreds of reuse cycles.
You will design, implement, and scale automated manufacturing processes that increase production rate, improve quality consistency, and reduce cost while maintaining the extreme reliability required for Starship. This role sits at the intersection of propulsion engineering, robotics, controls, and data systems.
Your work will directly enable rapid iteration and high-volume production of Raptor chambers and nozzles.

Develop, deploy and iteratively improve automated manufacturing systems for Raptor combustion chambers and nozzles, including robotic process automation and smart factory initiatives.
Implement process control and in-situ monitoring for the specialized manufacturing processes required to build the chamber and nozzle components.
Build and maintain data pipelines that capture manufacturing telemetry to enable statistical process control, predictive analytics, and machine learning models for defect reduction and process optimization.
Design fixture and material handling solutions that support chamber/nozzle build and assembly while maintaining tight geometric tolerances.
Drive continuous improvement of manufacturing automation through scripting (Python), PLC logic, and advanced process modeling to reduce cycle time and scrap rates.
Partner closely with propulsion design, materials, production, and supply chain teams to convert new designs into robust, scalable processes, resolve nonconformances, and drive design changes that improve manufacturability, reliability, and performance.
Establish version-controlled automation software with rigorous testing, ensuring manufacturing systems are reliable, repeatable, and safe.

Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline.
1+ years of experience automating manufacturing processes for metallic components.

Strong programming skills in Python and experience with industrial automation (PLC, LabVIEW, Beckhof, Siemens, Fanuc, ABB, Kuka).
Demonstrated experience with robotic systems, machine vision, or real-time process control in a manufacturing environment.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-ownership environment with aggressive schedules.
Ability to work well in an integrated and collaborative team environment including daily interactions with technicians, engineers, and managers.
Direct experience with rocket engine chamber or nozzle manufacturing (regeneratively cooled hardware is highly desired).
Expertise in machining, welding, precision assembly, or heat treatments.
Background in non-destructive inspection automation and closed-loop quality control.
Experience with large-scale data collection from manufacturing processes and building predictive models for defect detection or process optimization.
Familiarity with production systems and the unique challenges of scaling reusable rocket hardware.
Knowledge of geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T), precision metrology, and digital thread concepts.
Highly self-motivated with strong organizational and written/oral communication skills – able to prioritize and execute tasks in a high-pressure environment with the ongoing drive for continuous improvement in all aspects of work.

Our mission is to design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system, including thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that integrates it all.

You will be working with a multidisciplinary   team on efforts such as constructing a platform to test industrial ground antennas, high-power amplifiers, ground-to-space lasers, and more.

Ensure all software has an appropriate level of test coverage, balancing reliability, velocity and safety
Pioneer innovative strategies to scale the HITL fleet in accordance with the Starlink software organization’s growing test demands
Analyze and troubleshoot HITL test results to identify testbed issues and prevent software bugs from reaching production

This position is a test engineer for the Starship Structural Test team. This team develops, designs, builds, and executes large system-level static and dynamic structural tests.

Work with vehicle engineers, develop and execute static and dynamic system-level structural tests from conception. This includes test article and test stand configuration, boundary conditions, fluid, electrical, and software schematics, and concept of operations
Design, modify, and build mechanical systems. Systems include small lugs and brackets through large structural weldments
Design, modify, build, and troubleshoot fluid systems. Systems include low to high-pressure gaseous working fluids, rocket propellants (including cryogenic propellants), and hydraulic load control systems
Design, modify, build, and troubleshoot data acquisition (DAQ) and control systems, wiring, and instrumentation. DAQ systems are primarily NI-based, and instruments include strain gages, pressure transducers, deflection gages, load cells, thermocouples, and resistance temperature detectors (RTD)
Develop and maintain test procedures, sequences, scripts, configuration files, and software
Operate the test stand from test assembly and activation through test execution with a small team of engineers and technicians
Provide daily direction and instruction to technicians to integrate test articles and hardware (install instrumentation and wiring, assemble small and large mechanical components, repair metallic structures, pressurize and functional check pressure systems, lift and transport large structures)
Review data manually or using automatic scripts

1+ years of experience with testing, mechanical or data acquisition, and control system design (internships and college competition team count)

Demonstrated ability to learn new skills and adapt to new situations - unfazed by challenges that go beyond the traditional comfort zone or experience
Experience in project ownership under technical and schedule pressure, and where the scope and definition were limited
Experience testing and operating with or around hazardous systems (high pressure, high energy, hazardous gases and fluids, etc.)

s.t:
SpaceX is leveraging our experience building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s largest satellite constellation and most advanced broadband internet system.

We provide reliable and fast internet to millions of users worldwide, including populations with little or no connectivity, rural communities, aircraft, watercraft, and places where existing services are unreliable, too expensive, or disconnected by natural disasters.

We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system, thousands of satellites and consumer dishes that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing. The Starlink team is seeking out the best-in-class professionals to maximize Starlink’s potential for communities and businesses around the globe.
As a Thermal Mechanical Test Engineer for Silicon Packaging at SpaceX, you will develop and execute thermal and mechanical modeling and test programs for advanced semiconductor packaging and board-level assemblies. You will support the silicon packaging process engineering organization by characterizing package and board thermal performance, validating mechanical robustness, and correlating simulation results with physical test data to enable high-volume production of reliable Starlink hardware.

Develop and run thermal and mechanical finite element models, and thermal simulations, to predict package and board-level behavior under operational and environmental conditions
Develop process models to support new production line bring-up and investigations into packaging processes
Design, set up, and execute thermal and mechanical test campaigns
Perform board-level thermal characterization and testing to evaluate heat spreading, junction temperatures, and system-level thermal performance
Operate and maintain thermal and mechanical test equipment, such as thermal chambers, along with instrumentation, including thermocouples and infrared cameras
Analyze test data, correlate models with empirical results, and provide actionable feedback to packaging, silicon design, and manufacturing teams
Support new package and board designs through test planning, execution, and data reporting
Collaborate cross-functionally with packaging process engineers, hardware design teams, production operations, and quality to integrate test insights into product development and production ramp

Bachelor’s degree in an engineering, math, or science discipline
1+ years of experience with thermal or mechanical modeling and testing in an industry or academic setting

Bachelor’s in mechanical engineering, materials science, aerospace engineering, physics, applied mathematics, or other STEM discipline
Advanced degree in an engineering, math, or science discipline
Experience with board-level thermal testing and characterization using thermocouple mapping, power dissipation testing, or infrared thermography
Experience using finite element analysis or thermal simulation tools such as ANSYS, Abaqus, COMSOL, Flotherm, or Icepak
Experience with 3D and reduced-order thermal and mechanical modeling
Experience correlating simulation models with physical test data
Experience in simulation and characterization of IC packaging thermal resistance parameters
Proficiency in Python or MATLAB for data analysis and post-processing
Background in semiconductor packaging or high-reliability electronics environments
Experience working in a fast-paced, high-volume manufacturing or new product introduction setting
Ability to work extended hours or weekends as needed for mission critical deadlines

We are looking for a technically strong, hands-on QA Engineer to join our hardware team on-site at ODM factories in Taiwan.

This is not a checklist job - we're looking for someone who enjoys digging deep into technical issues, investigating root causes, and taking ownership of complex hardware problems.You'll be the key person ensuring the quality of our servers and racks before they ship, but more importantly, you'll play a critical role in debugging failures, analyzing test data, and working closely with RnD, logistics, and factory teams to continuously improve the process and the product.This is a deeply technical role that blends hardware validation, manufacturing QA, and problem-solving - perfect for someone who understands how servers are built and tested, and wants to make sure every unit that leaves the factory is production-grade.
What You'll Own
Technical Investigation & Debugging
Investigate complex problems (e.g., high GPU failure rate, power-related test failures), gather logs, run diagnostics, and escalate with context to RnD when needed.
Drive root cause analysis across factory teams and internal engineering groups.
Document findings and help define preventive actions for recurring problems.
Act as the first line of technical escalation for hardware issues discovered during factory QA or internal testing.Engineering Support
Participate in new platform bring-up sessions together with the visiting RnD teams during on-site trips to ODM labs.
Provide technical support, coordination, and hands-on assistance during the bring-up process.
Help ensure early-stage hardware behaves as expected, and escalate integration or platform issues to the relevant teams.On-Site Product QA
Perform visual inspections of completed products (servers, racks) before packaging.
Define and maintain QA checklists and inspection procedures tailored to different product lines.
Verify inventory records at the factory against internal system data (part numbers, serials, configurations).
Oversee the product packaging process for compliance with defined standards.
Supervise pickup operations: ensure outbound trucks meet shipment conditions and schedules.Failure Rate Monitoring & Analytics
Collect failure data from vendor-side burn-in and our own test systems.
Analyze failure trends and estimate spare part needs for future datacenter deployments.
Use dashboards and structured reporting to communicate insights with QA, engineering, and supply chain teams.Feedback Loop & Quality Improvement
Gather and process feedback from datacenters on each delivered batch of equipment:
* Report on packaging issues, impact sensor triggers, shipping anomalies.
* Assess rack-level build quality: cabling, bracket alignment, labeling.
* Log systemic hardware issues (design flaws, infant mortality, recurring failures).
Forward the feedback to the teams: logistics, ODM partners, hardware RnD, QA.Test Infrastructure & Validation
Assist with deployment and maintenance of test infrastructure on-site.
Ensure Nebius post-manufacturing hardware validation tests run smoothly (uptime, monitoring, coordination with support team).
Coordinate real-time issue escalation and basic triage with factory and internal teams.Local Insight & Communication
Communicate relevant local risks and context (e.g., typhoons, holidays, factory-specific constraints) to our global logistics and hardware teams.
Maintain productive relationships with factory staff, logistics providers, and internal stakeholders.
Working Conditions & Tools
During production peaks, issues may arise that require fast, hands-on debugging and resolution on-site. Flexibility is expected: you may need to stay late to investigate failures in freshly built batches or arrive early to verify and unblock outbound truck shipments. Rapid response and clear communication with engineering and factory teams are critical during these high-pressure periods.
Occasional international travel may be expected to Nebius headquarters in Amsterdam or to datacenters in Europe and the US.

* Managing workflows and escalation via Jira
* Writing and maintaining technical documentation in Confluence
* Using Grafana dashboards for monitoring test environments and system health
* Operating with several internal inventory and test control systems

Solid understanding of server and rack hardware: components, layout, cabling, power/cooling, diagnostics.
Ability to read and interpret technical documentation (e.g., datasheets, system specs, debug manuals).
Solid knowledge of electrical engineering fundamentals (e.g., power specs, grounding, signal integrity).
